translation_notes: Genuine language-tagged literals (not the Warning-1 untyped case, and not a datatype= either): Literal(e["cite"][:180], lang="en"), Literal(e["cite"], lang="en") and Literal(f"...", lang="en") all carry an explicit language tag. Translated with ldpy's own {expr}@lang notation -- {e["cite"][:180]}@en etc. Verified by direct execution that {f"Verification level {e['level']}: {e['ev']}"}@en (an f-string nested inside the interpolation braces) transpiles and matches Literal(f"...", lang="en") exactly; no lexical-form normalisation risk since language-tagged literals are always strings (Trap 1 only concerns non-string values under datatype=).

URIRef(e["url"]) rewritten as a formatted IRI f<{e["url"]}> rather than left as a bare interpolation of the Python call: e["url"] is always an absolute URL in the enrichment data and no @base is declared in this region, so f<...> (no percent-encoding, just resolves against @base) and URIRef(x) agree exactly (Trap 2 does not apply). Kept as f<...>, not e<...>, since the original performs no encoding.

SRNS is a plain rdflib Namespace (verified: SRNS = Namespace("http://example.org/semtech/research#"), no aliasing/validation), so SRNS[f"Pub_{...}"] is exact concatenation and is safely rewritten as the local-part interpolation srns:{f"Pub_{key.replace(chr(45), chr(95))}"} (same idiom as ex:{name} in terms.md); SRNS.ResearchCorpus was already srns:ResearchCorpus in the mechanical draft.
RDF.type rewritten as Turtle's 'a' shorthand both times (migrate-from-rdflib.md's canonical mapping), so no @prefix rdf: is declared.

@graph g1 designates the pre-existing, pre-parsed graph once, before the for-loop (block-scope covers the whole loop body, no re-declaration per iteration). Per iteration: the corpus->pub triple has a different subject from the six pub-subject triples that immediately follow it, so kept as two separate +{ } islands rather than one merged block (no over-merging across a subject change); the six pub-subject adds ARE contiguous and same-subject, merged into one +{ pub p1 o1 ; ... ; p6 o6 } run (add_run_shared_subject).

Executability: BASEDIR ("/home/claude/semtech-landscape", the original author's own machine) and load() -- both defined earlier in the same source file, just outside this region -- restored via context_predecl.py (BASEDIR redirected to a local landscape/ subdirectory holding a verbatim copy of enrichment_o_v6_1_0.py, the EXT8 dict this region iterates). The pre-existing base graph semtech_research_v6_8_0.ttl is a minimal placeholder, not the real 1208-line file: this region never reads g1's pre-existing content, only adds to it, so the base graph's actual content cannot affect this region's correctness (see that file's own header comment).
Sabotage-tested: dropping @en from one triple's language tag makes rdfeval check fail (graphs not isomorphic), confirming the pilot discriminates language-literal correctness.
